title: elastic-reserve-portfolio-pricing-sketch
body:
Goal
-----
Sketch a lightweight, copy-and-edit friendly model + recommendation checklist for selling and operating reserved GPU pools as a portfolio product offer (mix of GPU classes, regions, and start/stop windows). Focus is on heuristics that non-finance folks can use to reason about pricing and utilization tradeoffs and to create quick scenario stress-tests in a spreadsheet.

Context + motivation
--------------------
- Sales asks: customers want predictable monthly $ cap and the ability to grow/shrink without major re-negotiation.
- Ops asks: we need to maximize multi-tenant utilization while keeping SLOs for committed customers.
- Finance asks: present break-even formulas and downside protection (idle sink, churn) without exposing overly complex Monte Carlo models.

High-level idea
---------------
Treat a reserved commitment as a small portfolio of capacity blocks. Each portfolio mixes: (A) base long-term reservations (cheapest per-GPU), (B) mid-term staggered starts (lower discount), and (C) short-term burst credit (premium). Price per portfolio as a blended unit cost + optional premium for guaranteed headroom.

Key levers captured in the model
--------------------------------
- Commit term (12/24/36 months) -> clearance discount curve
- GPU class mix -> per-hour amortization rate (A100-80C, H100, RTX6000 etc)
- Region premium -> delta multiplier (us-west, eu-central, apac)
- Pool overcommit factor -> expected utilization / SLA buffer
- Burst credits allocation -> effective on-demand offset
- Onboarding lag / ramp assumptions (pct of committed capacity used in month 1..6)

Suggested spreadsheet layout (one row = one portfolio commitment)
------------------------------------------------------------------
Columns: Portfolio ID | Customer | Start month | Term months | GPU class mix | Committed vGPU hrs/mo | Expected util pct | Amortized cost/mo | Energy+infra/mo | Blended per-GPU-hr | Buffer reserve (hrs) | Burst credits/mo | Effective unit price | Suggested list price | Break-even utilization

Example row (illustrative)
--------------------------
P-2025-01 | AcmeAI | 2025-04 | 24 | 70% H100, 30% A100 | 43,200 hrs | 72% | $45,000 | $6,200 | $1.20/hr | 1,200 hrs | 4,000 credits | $1.45/hr | $1.80/hr | 64%

Core formulas (plain text)
--------------------------
- amortized_cost/mo = (purchase_price * (1 - resale_adj)) / term_months + ops_overhead
- blended_per_gpu_hr = amortized_cost/mo / (committed_hrs * expected_util_pct)
- effective_unit_price = blended_per_gpu_hr * (1 + ops_target_margin)
- break_even_util = amortized_cost/mo / (committed_hrs * forecasted_price_per_hr)

Sensitivity knobs to include in the sheet (input cells)
-------------------------------------------------------
- Idle penalty multiplier (how much idle time actually costs vs theoretical)
- Churn shock scenario: percent of portfolio canceled at 6/12/18 months and recompute pool-level utilization + immediate cash impact
- Spot/market hedge: fraction of capacity replaced with spot/preemptable + expected eviction rate
- Cross-customer pooling factor (allocable slack across customers)

Operational heuristics / pricing plays (recommendations)
-------------------------------------------------------
1) Staggered-start discount tapering: offer 2–3 tranche prices rather than single mono-price; this reduces tail-idle risk when customers ramp late.
2) Buffer credit product: bake small amount of burst credits into all tiers; charge for overage. Helps reduce SLA/penalty exposure while monetizing peaks.
3) Commitment smoothing step: require 30–60 days notice for >20% downsizes; allow one small (<=10%) shrink per year free.
4) Dynamic overcommit bands: set target utilization band (e.g., 65–80%) and automatically switch low-util portfolios into a secondary market pool for backfill when below threshold.
5) Regional price deltas: use region multiplier table rather than trying to rebalance hardware across regions monthly.

Quick scenario outputs to surface to sales and SRE
------------------------------------------------
- Portfolio blended unit price 
- Pool-level utilization and idle-hours (monthly)
- Marginal cost to serve 1 additional 1K GPU-hrs (with vs without burst credits)
- 12-month cash runway impact of a 20% churn event on newest vs oldest commitments

Mini stress test (copy into spreadsheet)
-------------------------------------
Assumptions: total committed = 200k hrs/mo, average util = 70%, amortized_cost = $200k/mo, burst credits = 20k hrs
- Baseline unit cost = 200k / (200k * 0.7) = $1.43/hr
- If churn 20% of committed disappears and we can only reallocate 50% cross-customer immediately: new util = (0.8*200k * 0.7 + 0.2*200k * 0.35) / 200k = 0.61 -> unit cost = 200k / (200k * 0.61) = $1.64/hr -> ~15% unit cost increase

Open questions / assumptions to validate
--------------------------------------
- Resale price / secondary market assumptions for hardware after term end
- True marginal infra costs at different utilization bands (we use linear model today; might be concave)
- Realistic eviction rates if we lean on spot for 10–30% of capacity
- Legal / contract constraints around multi-customer pooling in certain regulated accounts

Immediate next actions (owner: Priya)
------------------------------------
- Build a companion spreadsheet with the column layout above and prefilled example rows; include toggles for churn shock and spot mix (Due: 2024-11-15)
- Run 3 historical rewind scenarios using last 18 months of Dedicated telemetry to calibrate idle penalty multiplier (owner: Marcus) (Due: 2024-11-22)
- Draft a 1-page sales cheat sheet with bullets for pricing options and recommended negotiation levers (owner: Samir) (Due: 2024-11-29)

Notes to self / rough thoughts
----------------------------
- Keep model understandable: one-tab inputs, one-tab outputs, one-tab raw rows. Sales should be able to toggle 3 knobs and give a ballpark in 5 mins.
- Consider adding a "credit escrow" concept where unused burst credits roll forward up to 3 months to reduce churn friction.

Links to related artifacts
-------------------------
- See provisioning-runbook for pool backfill rules (link internal)
- Dataset: dedicated-telemetry/usage-2023-2025 (for calibration)

End of sketch.
